title: Sections and strict presentations of enhanced cocartesian fibrations
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, cores and universes from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian and cocartesian fibrations and their edges and fibres from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Opposite simplicial sets reverse the ordering of vertices and interchange the $i$th and $(n-i)$th faces.

For a map $p:X\to S$, the simplicial set of sections has $r$-simplices the maps $S\times\Delta^r\to X$ whose composite with $p$ is the projection to $S$, with operators given by precomposition in the second factor. For a cocartesian fibration write $\Gamma_{\mathrm{cocart}}(S,X)$ for the full simplicial subset on sections carrying every edge of $S$ to a $p$-cocartesian edge. Thus higher simplices include arbitrary transformations over $S$ between those sections; their components need not be equivalences. Cartesian sections are defined dually. Write $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ for the homotopy coherent nerve [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] of the simplicial category whose objects are the quasicategories in a universe containing all the fibres under discussion and whose mapping spaces are the cores of their internal functor simplicial sets, with composition induced by composition of functors; it is formed in a further containing universe, as in Lecture II of the six-functor notes.

Let $C$ be a small ordinary category and let $D$ be a strict functor from $C$ to such quasicategories: simplicial maps $D(f):D(c)\to D(d)$ for arrows $f:c\to d$, with $D(\mathrm{id}_c)=\mathrm{id}$ and $D(gf)=D(g)D(f)$. Regarding $C$ as a simplicial category with discrete mapping spaces, $D$ is a simplicial functor, and its homotopy coherent nerve is a diagram $N(C)\to\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, still written $D$. The marked Grothendieck construction $G_C(D)$ is the simplicial set whose $n$-simplices are pairs $(\sigma,\tau)$ of a functor $\sigma:[n]\to C$ and an $n$-simplex $\tau$ of $D(\sigma(0))$; a monotone $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ sends $(\sigma,\tau)$ to $(\sigma\theta,D(\sigma(0)\to\sigma(\theta(0)))(\theta^*\tau))$. Projection to $\sigma$ is a map $G_C(D)\to N(C)$ whose fibre over $c$ is $D(c)$. An edge $(f,\tau)$ is marked when $\tau$ is degenerate, $\tau=s_0x$; it then runs from $x$ to $D(f)(x)$. Over each simplex of $N(C)$ this is the mapping simplex of the corresponding composable string, with cocartesian variance; $G_C(D)\to N(C)$ need not be an inner fibration. For a cocartesian fibration $q:Q\to N(C)$ of quasicategories, a strict presentation of $q$ by $D$ is a simplicial map $\varphi:G_C(D)\to Q$ over $N(C)$ that carries every marked edge to a $q$-cocartesian edge and restricts, for every object $c$, to an equivalence of quasicategories $D(c)\to Q\times_{N(C)}\{c\}$.

source.place: Proposition 7.4.4.1 (Tag 05RX), the category of cocartesian sections. Mapping simplex and its marking: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Section 3.2.2, the mapping simplex definition and Notation 3.2.2.3 (printed pp. 179-180), dualized to cocartesian variance.
